posts.title: Earth Magic
posts.description: A review of Nature Boy’s Magical World by CJ Stone Steve Andrews Steve Andrews, the author of this book and regular contributor to Whitstable Views, is one of my oldest friends. We’ve known each other since 1971, when I first went to University in Cardiff. Steve was a local, having been brought up in Llandaff, a posh suburb on the outskirts of the city. We are about the same age, both born in 1953. Steve is a little older than me, having arrived in the world in March, while I popped out in June. He was born on the equinox, while my birthday is nearing the solstice. We grew up in the same ethos. Young hippies, looking to the recent stirrings in California in the mid-sixties for inspiration. Peace, love and Rock’n’Roll. Drugs. Psychedelia. Flares. Long hair. Trench coats. Tie-dye. Spirituality. Wholefood. All that shit. posts.title: Whitstable twins inspire Christmas picture book as their aunt fulfils a childhood dream
posts.description: Photo: Lucy Miles-Barnes with A Christmas Wish. Lilah and Posie, the twins who inspired Lulu and Pop. The arrival of identical twin nieces Lilah and Posie in 2020 inspired Lucy Miles-Barnes to turn her childhood dream of writing children’s books into a collection of woodland adventures. Now her Christmas picture book, A Christmas Wish , has been published with a special family tribute. Written and illustrated by Lucy, the book is part of her Twin Tails series and follows twin mouse sisters Lulu and Pop. On Christmas Eve, they make a wish on a star. A tiny letter leads them into the snowy woods, where Father Mousemas has a surprise waiting. Aimed at children aged four to eight, the story celebrates sisterhood, kindness and Christmas magic. The real twins behind the inspiration are now six and live in Whitstable with their mum, Lucy’s sister Laura Miles. posts.title: Job losses expected As National Express axes Kent to London coach routes
posts.description: With Petition Two major National Express coach routes linking East Kent with London are set to be scrapped next month, putting up to 20 jobs in jeopardy and threatening a local depot with closure. From December 7, the 007 service—which connects Dover, Folkestone, and Canterbury with the capital—and the 022 route serving Ramsgate, Margate, Canterbury, and London will cease operating. Passengers holding advance bookings for dates after December 7 will be contacted regarding the cancellations and offered refunds where applicable. The withdrawals carry severe consequences for local transport workers, who were informed of the cuts last week. While National Express operates the routes, the coaches and drivers are managed by partner company Coach Travel Group (CTG) from a depot on Pike Road in Eythorne, near Dover.
